def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Returns the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using a max-heap approach.
    The time complexity is O(n + k log n) due to heap operations.
    """
    import heapq

    # Create a min-heap of the k largest elements
    min_heap = []
    
    for num in nums:
        if len(min_heap) < k:
            heapq.heappush(min_heap, num)
        else:
            heapq.heappushpop(min_heap, num)
    
    return min_heap[0]

def kth_largest(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    """
    Returns the k-th largest element in an unsorted list using the Heap Select algorithm.
    The time complexity is O(n + k log n) where n is the number of elements in the input list.
    """
    import heapq

    # Create a min-heap with the first k elements
    min_heap = nums[:k]
    heapq.heapify(min_heap)

    # Iterate through the rest of the elements
    for num in nums[k:]:
        if num > min_heap[0]:  # If the current number is larger than the smallest in the heap
            heapq.heappop(min_heap)  # Remove the smallest
            heapq.heappush(min_heap, num)  # Add the current number to the heap

    return min_heap[0]  # The root of the min-heap is the k-th largest element
